title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: WADE'S BOXES
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Wade Kessler, a propane truck driver in Rapid City, South Dakota.
He has not finished a book since the days of dial-up.
Then his dad moved to Florida and left him eleven boxes of them.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE BOXES
segments.quote: Some books are to be tasted, others to be swallowed, and some few to be chewed and digested.
segments.author: Francis Bacon
lines: Wade stacked the boxes and called it a coffee table.
His dad Hank called from Tampa and said, Read one. Then call me.
Wade said, Dad, there are four hundred books here. Hank read him a line from Francis Bacon:
Some books are to be tasted, others to be swallowed, and some few to be chewed and digested.
So Wade read the first page of twenty books, and kept three.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE BIG ONE
segments.quote: A man ought to read just as inclination leads him; for what he reads as a task will do him little good.
segments.author: Samuel Johnson
lines: He started with the fattest one, to look smart. He fell asleep on page nine. Three nights running.
Inside the cover, in Dad's handwriting, was a line from Samuel Johnson:
A man ought to read just as inclination leads him; for what he reads as a task will do him little good.
So Wade swapped it for a beat-up cowboy story.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE WAITING ROOM
segments.quote: Books are a uniquely portable magic.
segments.author: Stephen King
lines: That week he sat two hours in a tire shop. On the back of the book, a line from Stephen King:
Books are a uniquely portable magic.
Wade opened it, and the tire shop turned into Texas, eighteen eighty.
When they called his name, he asked if they could take a little longer.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BARBERSHOP
segments.quote: Reading furnishes the mind only with materials of knowledge; it is thinking that makes what we read ours.
segments.author: John Locke
lines: His barber Benny ran a Tuesday book club. Wade said, I just read. I don't think about it.
Benny pointed his scissors at a line from John Locke, taped to the mirror:
Reading furnishes the mind only with materials of knowledge; it is thinking that makes what we read ours.
Ten minutes later, Wade argued about the ending so loud, Benny cut his sideburns crooked.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE PHONE CALL
segments.author: Thomas Jefferson
lines: On Sunday Wade called Dad. They talked two hours. About a book.
Wade asked, Why give them all away? Hank said, Thomas Jefferson once wrote,
I cannot live without books.
But I can live without them a while, if it gets my son to call.
Wade mailed him the cowboy story, to read together.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE WORKOUT
segments.quote: Reading is to the mind what exercise is to the body.
segments.author: Joseph Addison
lines: Now Wade reads every lunch break. The guys at the depot teased him,
so he taped up a line from Joseph Addison:
Reading is to the mind what exercise is to the body.
His gym card is untouched. But his mind? Bench pressing two hundred pages a week.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Taste a few. Read what you love. Find the magic. Think it over. Call home. Keep at it.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Taste a few. Read what you love. Find the magic. Think it over. Call home. Keep at it.
Me? I read in bed every night. The same page, all week.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
